name: Transverse Vaginal Septum

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Transverse Vaginal Septum

criteria.description: Primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain in adolescent females
Palpable vaginal obstruction or shortened vaginal canal on gynecological examination
Ultrasound or MRI demonstrating transverse vaginal septum with proximal vaginal distension
Exclusion of other causes of vaginal obstruction such as imperforate hymen or vaginal agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain, physical evidence of vaginal obstruction, and imaging confirmation of transverse vaginal septum
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; histopathology may be used post-surgically.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain
Palpable transverse vaginal septum on gynecological examination

common.symptomName: Hematocolpos (accumulation of menstrual blood behind septum)
Difficulty with tampon insertion or vaginal intercourse
Urinary retention or dysuria due to mass effect

pain due to pressure on spine

laboratory: Normal hormonal profile (FSH, LH, estrogen) unless associated anomalies present
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing hematocolpos or hematometra
MRI pelvis confirming location and thickness of transverse vaginal septum
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Physical exam revealing vaginal obstruction or shortened vaginal canal

distinguishingFeatures: Imperforate hymen presents with bulging hymenal membrane at vaginal introitus
Usually diagnosed at menarche with hematocolpos
Absent or rudimentary uterus and upper two-thirds of vagina
Primary amenorrhea without cyclic pelvic pain

redFlags: Severe cyclic pelvic pain with primary amenorrhea
Progressive abdominal or pelvic mass suggesting hematocolpos or hematometra
Urinary retention or recurrent urinary tract infections
